inputs.prompt: Use the image as the authority for density, materials and design language, and recompose it as a tall vertical frame: a low camera just above the surface of a vast sea of red, yellow, blue and green ball-pit balls, looking steeply up into the structure as it rises out of sight. A colossal indoor children's play place that never ends, designed like a liminal dream: a dense knotted tangle of enclosed tube slides in faded red, orange, blue and green snaking in every direction, looping around each other, plunging through towers and out the other side, joined by sagging rope-net bridges and crawl tunnels, caged climbing towers of green-painted steel mesh, clusters of clear plastic bubble pods, padded platforms, ladders, junction boxes where five tubes meet. Every gap is filled with another tube or another bridge; there is no empty air. The same play modules repeat into the distance in every direction, smaller and smaller, forever, until they dissolve into haze. No floor and no ceiling are visible except the ball sea far below. The mood is uncanny, airless and wrong: perfectly still and empty, immaculate but abandoned, as if the place has been waiting for decades. Pools of deep black shadow swallow whole sections. Lighting is sickly sodium-yellow and buzzing pale fluorescent tubes in places, with single deep-crimson warning lamps glowing in the dark, a few amber caged practicals, and cold blue haze between it all. Faded yellowed vinyl padding with water stains, scuffed plastic, slightly too-saturated color. Faint smoke in the air. Photographic 35mm film still, 1990s film grain, slight halation, deep contrast. No people, no figures, no mascots, no text, no signage, no logos.
